_comment: THE WEEKLY LETTER'S OWN CAPABILITY CONTRACT.
WHY THIS IS NOT deploy/loop_settings.json. Three roles shared that one
file — the trading session, the exit executor and the newsletter — so every
capability any of them needed, all of them got. Their authority is not the
same: a session decides what to hold, the exit executor places exits
somebody else already decided on, and THE NEWSLETTER WRITES PROSE. Its
intended authority over live money is ZERO. Under the shared file it held
mcp__robinhood-trading__place_equity_order and cancel_equity_order, with
the Robinhood server mounted — a narrating process with a live order
surface. Nothing is known to have used it. That is not the same as it being
safe: the general order gate ALLOWS every sell by design (refusing one
would strip a fractional position of its only stop), so a sell from this
process would have passed the gate and reached the broker.
The removal is MECHANICAL, not a matter of the prompt being asked to
behave: deploy/newsletter_mcp.json declares NO MCP servers and
--strict-mcp-config makes it the only source, so no broker tool exists to
call. The order-tool denies at the bottom of this file are belt-and-braces
against a future edit that mounts one; they are not what closes the hole.
THERE IS NO `hooks` KEY, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The PreToolUse order gate
exists to stand in front of place_equity_order. This process has no such
tool — nothing to gate. Adding the gate here would imply an order path that
must not exist.
PERMISSIONS = EXACTLY WHAT prompts/newsletter.md DOES, path by path:
step 1   Read research_store/newsletters/facts.json — every figure in the
letter comes from it, and the prompt forbids computing one.
step 1   Bash `.venv/bin/python scripts/letter_facts.py` — the prompt's
named fallback for a missing facts file. deploy/run_newsletter.sh
runs it first, so this is the safety net, not the normal path.
It is the ONE permitted command and it is spelled in full: a bare
`Bash` grant, or a bare `Bash` in --allowedTools, would make it
'may run anything' (probed on this box — see scripts/
market_monitor.py:EXECUTOR_TOOLS for the same finding).
step 2   Read newsletter/template.html — the {{TOKEN}} skeleton it fills.
step 3   Write research_store/newsletters/issue_<N>.html — THE ONLY
artifact it produces — then Read it back to verify no `{{`
remains. Scoped to issue_*.html rather than the directory so it
cannot overwrite facts.json, which is its own source of truth.
step 3b  Read + Edit docs/OPSLOG.md — the week's operational material is
PREPENDED there rather than put in the letter (Aaron's standing
instruction, 2026-07-10: the letter states portfolio impact in
one sentence and points here). ⚠️ 'Prepend, never replace' is the
PROMPT's instruction, not a guarantee this file makes: as the
Edit(...)-vs-Write(...) note below explains, an Edit(path) rule
authorises the Write tool on that path too, so the rule permits a
wholesale rewrite of OPSLOG.md that the procedure forbids. The
file is in git; that is what makes the difference recoverable.
step 4   the letter does NOT send itself. deploy/run_newsletter.sh runs
scripts/send_newsletter.py after the model exits, so the
credentials and the network never enter this surface at all.
Nothing else is listed. The launcher runs --permission-mode dontAsk, which
DECIDES rather than hanging on a prompt nobody is there to answer, and it
passes --tools "Read,Write,Edit,Bash", so WebFetch, WebSearch and the rest
of the built-in set are ABSENT from this process, not merely unpermitted.
⚠️ dontAsk IS NOT A PURE AUTO-DENY — measured under this exact
configuration on 2026-08-23, not assumed. Every write and every network
command off the list was refused (touch, curl, rm facts.json, cat .env,
any write outside research_store/newsletters/), but the CLI auto-approved
some read-only in-repo commands it judges safe (`git status --short`,
`wc -l`) while refusing others (`ls -l`, `git ls-files`). What this file
plus that mode actually guarantee is: CANNOT MUTATE ANYTHING NOT LISTED
ABOVE, AND CANNOT REACH THE NETWORK. That is the claim to rely on. The
letter loses nothing by the gap — it has no broker tool and no egress —
but do not read `Bash(...)` here as the complete list of what may run.
⛔ EVERY FILE RULE HERE IS SPELLED Edit(...), AND NONE IS SPELLED Write(...).
That is not a typo and it is not stylistic. Probed against the installed CLI
(2.1.241, this box, 2026-08-23): a path-scoped `Write(path)` rule is NOT
matched by file permission checks, and the CLI says so on stderr for every
such rule, every run — 'only Edit(path) rules are. Use Edit(path) instead
(Edit rules cover all file-editing tools)'. An earlier draft of this file
carried 19 of them; the Write TOOL was in fact being authorised by the
Edit(...) rule sitting next to it, and the Write(...) rules enforced nothing
while making the file LOOK locked. `Edit(...)` covers the Write tool as well
as Edit, which is why one rule per path is both correct and sufficient.
deploy/loop_settings.json recorded this same finding on 2026-08-11; it is
restated here because a future editor adding a path will reach for Write().
⛔ THE DENY BLOCK IS THE FLOOR, NOT THE CEILING. Deny beats allow, so these
hold even if the allow list above is widened by a later edit: no secrets,
no repo code, no config, no launcher, no prompts, and none of the research
store the trading system actually runs on — the belief file, the journal,
the monitor's control files, the price panel. The letter reads a facts file
and writes an HTML file; it has no business editing the system it reports
on. docs/ is deliberately NOT denied wholesale, because OPSLOG.md above
needs to be editable and a blanket deny would silently win over it.
